_readme: The wire contract for a single memory as returned by the REST API.
(and any other client that hand-declares the shape)
Both sides are checked against `keys` by a test — rest_api.rs's
src/contract.test.ts. Adding, renaming or removing a field therefore
requires editing this file, which is the point: it is the one place
where a change to the shape has to be declared out loud before either
side can be updated to match.
Before this file existed the plugin's interface was a hand-kept copy
that had drifted to 10 of 24 fields with nothing watching it. Every
change happened to be additive, so nothing broke — but a rename would
have arrived as `undefined` and been written into note frontmatter as
`keys` is sorted and must stay sorted; both tests assert that, so a
merge that inserts a field in the wrong place fails loudly rather
_renames_readme: wire name -> name the consumer uses. `memory_to_json` renames the
struct's `memory_type` to `type` (as does the struct's own serde
attribute); the Obsidian plugin renames it back in main.ts's
listMemories adapter so the rest of the plugin reads `memory_type`.
contract.test.ts applies this map before comparing.
_omitted_readme: Fields on the Rust `Memory` struct that memory_to_json deliberately
does NOT expose. Listed so the omission is a decision on the record
rather than an accident, and so rest_api.rs can assert that every
struct field is either in `keys` or here — a newly added field that
lands in neither fails the test instead of silently staying invisible.

identity_verified is exposed as read-only evidence of the persisted write,
not as request authority and never inferred from the current registry.
